tier_reason: Independent third-party harness, not by the aubio project (faroit/python_audio_loading_benchmark: benchmark_np.py, benchmark_metadata.py and loaders.py are public; its authors are faroit and hagenw, and librosa maintainer bmcfee re-ran the wav load). Its results/*.pickle files hold numbers that rank aubio ahead of audioread's ffmpeg-subprocess reader and librosa. It falls short of A: there is no CPU model, OS or build configuration ('our server', 'my dev machine'), and aubio 0.4.9 is an sdist-only package whose decoder backend depends on the build. Tier B follows the pigzbench precedent.

corrections.baseline: audioread (FFmpegAudioFile for the load benchmark, audioread.audio_open with its auto-selected backend for the metadata benchmark; compressed formats decode through an ffmpeg subprocess)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Numbers derived from the benchmark's results/*.pickle files (derived from page data; mean over the 16 durations). Load rows are the minimum of 3 timeit repeats of 3 loads of one file per duration. Load to numpy, aubio vs audioread+ffmpeg: wav 0.064 vs 0.657 s (about 10x; this wav row comes from bmcfee's Feb 2023 dev-machine run), mp4 0.044 vs 0.101 (about 2.3x), mp3 0.068 vs 0.103 (about 1.5x), flac 0.067 vs 0.071 (about 1.06x, a tie). Versus librosa: mp3 0.068 vs 0.131 (about 1.9x), mp4 0.044 vs 0.111 (about 2.5x), wav 0.064 vs 0.289 (about 4.5x). Versus soundfile on wav: 0.064 vs 0.103. Metadata rows are seconds per info call, and each call opens the file 4 times. Aubio vs audioread: mp3 0.0015 vs 0.098 (about 66x), flac 0.0015 vs 0.098 (about 66x), mp4 0.0030 vs 0.106 (about 35x), ogg 0.0046 vs 0.200 (about 44x), wav 0.040 vs 0.099 (about 2.5x). Aubio is slower in several rows. Flac load: 0.067 vs soundfile 0.045 and librosa 0.039. Wav load: 0.064 vs scipy 0.014. Metadata vs torchaudio: flac 0.0015 vs 0.000062, mp3 0.0015 vs 0.00054, ogg 0.0046 vs 0.00063, wav 0.040 vs 0.000039. Metadata vs soundfile: flac 0.0015 vs 0.00053, ogg 0.0046 vs 0.0041, wav 0.040 vs 0.0008. Aubio has no row in the ogg load pickle.
corrections.caveats: This is an independent community benchmark (faroit/python_audio_loading_benchmark, 152 stars, last commit 2023-12-19), not run by the aubio project. The README shows only bar charts on a log time axis; the exact numbers come from the repo's results/benchmark_np_<ext>.pickle and benchmark_metadata_<ext>.pickle files, read with a restricted unpickler that whitelists pandas and numpy classes and executes no code. The numbers mix two runs on different machines. PR #8 (merged 2021-09-06, faroit's 'server') produced every pickle except np_wav, with 2020-21 library versions (librosa 0.8 era). PR #26 (bmcfee's 'dev machine', merged 2023-12-19) replaced only results/benchmark_np_wav.pickle, with librosa 0.10, soundfile 0.12.1 and scipy 1.9. The README version table therefore describes only the wav load row, and the README charts were not regenerated after #26 ('create new plots later'). On that machine ffmpeg was slow to start: audioread took at least 0.28 s for 3 loads of a 1 s wav file, against 0.024 s for flac in the 2021 run, which inflates the 10x wav ratio. The repo states no hardware, CPU model, OS or compiler. The Dockerfile (python:3.6.8) cannot install the pinned tensorflow 2.11 and librosa 0.10, and bmcfee reported the docker instructions failing, so the environment is not reproducible as published. The aubio package's build configuration (whether its decoder backend is libav) is not stated; aubio 0.4.9 (2019-02-08, still the latest PyPI release) ships only as an sdist. Harness quirks: the load benchmark records the minimum of 3 timeit repeats with number=3 (seconds for 3 loads) and keeps only the last file of each duration folder. The metadata benchmark records the mean seconds per info call over every file and 3 rounds, and each info call opens the file 4 times. The audioread baseline spawns an ffmpeg process per file (FFmpegAudioFile for loads, audio_open's auto-selected backend for metadata), so aubio's win is largely process-spawn overhead rather than faster codecs; aubio itself decodes mp3/mp4 through libav (FFmpeg's libraries) when built with it. Aubio is a competitive loader, not the fastest one. libsndfile (soundfile), scipy and librosa beat it on wav or flac loads, and torchaudio and soundfile beat it on most metadata queries (torchaudio by 2-1000x). Aubio's own repo has only python/demos/demo_reading_speed.py with no published numbers, and its README makes no speed claim. The 'ffmpeg or standard codec' baseline was a Haiku guess; the rows compared here are audioread's ffmpeg wrapper, not the ffmpeg library called from C.

notes: All claimed numbers match the pickles; I re-derived them myself. Confirmed at B as an independent harness. Shortcomings: the win is over an ffmpeg-subprocess wrapper, so it is mostly spawn overhead. The data mixes a 2023 wav-only rerun on bmcfee's dev machine with 2021 server runs for the other formats. No hardware is stated and the Docker setup is broken. torchaudio and soundfile beat aubio on most metadata rows, and soundfile, librosa and scipy beat it on flac or wav loads. Metadata confirmed: GPL-3.0-or-later, 3.8k stars, last commit 2026-04-10, not a fork, not archived.
